header.reason: Martin, the CFO, saw only a rate comparison and no figure for what failed orders cost Fernbrook. Sam blames price, but nothing on the page showed we weren't 'the same thing'.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Lead with big orders failing at checkout, not average acceptance gains.

line.text: Authorization Boost increases acceptance rates by 3.8% on average

findings.why: Lucy came inbound because about one in twelve online orders failed, worst on the biggest baskets.
findings.quote: about one in twelve online orders was failing at the payment step

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Tell the finance lead what failed orders cost, not just our rate.
findings.why: Sam never met Martin, who only saw a rate page and called us 'the same thing'.
findings.quote: Lucy told me. I never met him.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Say what stays broken when they only get a better rate.
findings.why: Per Lucy via Sam, the bank cut its rate but offered no fix for failing orders.
findings.quote: No new product, nothing. Just a better rate.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Keep explaining why big orders get declined and how we fix it.

line.text: Adaptive Acceptance adjusts the payment request and retries declines in real time

findings.why: Lucy nodded through Farah's explanation, while the average uplift slide never reached Martin.
findings.quote: Lucy was nodding the whole way.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Add a one-page cost of failed orders in the customer's own numbers.
findings.why: Lucy asked for a business case to hand Martin but got the deck and average uplift.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Say 'orders dying at the last step' instead of 'acceptance rates'.

line.text: Authorization Boost increases acceptance rates by 3.8% on average

findings.why: Lucy described her problem as losing big orders at checkout, not as rates.
findings.quote: orders dying at the last step
